**What broke:** Last Thursday (Nov 12, 08:47–12:27 UTC, ~3h40), the ingest-worker pods started OOM-looping right after the v2.14.0 deploy, which raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB (PR ingest#412) while the pods had only a 512 Mi memory limit [10][1]. Consumer lag exceeded 500,000 messages, with out-of-memory allocation errors in `ingest/worker/batch.go` [4]. Initially suspected Kafka broker disk, but that was ruled out [10]. Customer dashboards showed stale data, up to ~3h40 behind at peak [1][10].

**Data loss:** None. Reconciliation on Nov 13 matched event counts per workspace against Kafka offsets for the affected window — "nothing lost, just late" [10][1]. The customer report to Orbitly confirms the same [2].

**What's changing:**
- A new alert routed to on-call when ingest consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Linear KES-431, due Nov 20) [12][2]
- Configuration changes will go to a small canary group first before full rollout [2]
- The postmortem also mentions "mo…" (likely more items) in Maya's report [2], and the full list is in Lior's postmortem page [1]

Side note: the team also postponed the Nov 21 Postgres 17 cutover to avoid stacking risk right after the incident [3], and Orbitly is claiming an SLA service credit per MSA section 7, which Sam is checking with finance [2].
